## Baseline authority and interpretation

This is the single source-derived baseline for the TrafficTwin v0.8 traceability audit. It describes the negotiated MSc/project obligations that can be defended from the accessible evidence; it is not a union of product ideas and it does not derive requirements from implementation.

The official Project 237 brief remains the only authoritative substantive project scope and has not been shown to be formally superseded (S-001). Later supervisor notes plausibly specialise that scope toward comparative RSU load management, but the decisive 4 August Outlook email is unavailable and the surviving records are class C (S-011, S-012). Accordingly, the formal brief remains MUST, the late RSU specialisation is SHOULD with an open decision, and the data-engineering/what-if platform is MAY because the latest accessible platform-specific supervisor note places it after the scientific work, if time permits (S-008–S-010).

Priority terms have their ordinary audit meaning: MUST is required by authoritative or confirmed evidence, including explicitly triggered legal/ethical/semantic constraints; SHOULD is a well-supported expected outcome whose final authority or minimum scope remains incomplete; MAY is optional. A conditional MUST is evaluated only when its stated trigger occurs.

## Included source record

- Complete corpus considered: S-001 through S-034 (34 unique sources: 5 A, 2 B, 7 C, 14 D, 6 E).
- Direct active-requirement basis: S-001, S-002, S-003, S-004, S-005, S-006, S-007, S-008, S-009, S-010, S-011, S-012, S-017, S-018.
- Decision-history, exclusion, or unresolved-permission basis additionally cited: S-013, S-014, S-015, S-016, S-019, S-020, S-021, S-022, S-023, S-024, S-025, S-026, S-027, S-028, S-029, S-030, S-031, S-032, S-033, S-034.
- Class D and E sources do not establish active MUST requirements. Their presence here records exclusions, provenance, owner intent, supersession, or unresolved decisions only.

## Concise negotiation history

1. The 27 May 2026 official Project 237 brief established a resource-management-centred ITS project: investigate a suitable methodology, implement a few ITS use cases, profile their run-time behaviour, assess existing cloud resource-management strategies against service/QoS needs, and propose improved dynamic strategies across devices and clouds (S-001).
2. Official programme material added assessment, report/video, evaluation, technical-accuracy, and conditional ethics obligations, not TrafficTwin product features (S-002–S-004).
3. Early supervision explored alternatives. A heterogeneous traffic data-engineering/current-view/forecasting/what-if platform was initially only a possibility; a Manchester digital-twin-style app was later described as a candidate while task offloading versus journey-time prediction remained undecided (S-008, S-009).
4. Randy proposed monitoring, dashboard, explainability, and resource-advice ideas but expressly conditioned development on Sandra's approval; no acceptance of that complete product concept is evidenced (S-015, S-016).
5. Meeting 3 prioritised scientific explanation and validation of the counter-intuitive experiment and demoted the data platform to a small extension after the core work, if time remained (S-010).
6. Abdulla subsequently chose the platform as a product-owner direction, and internal designs elaborated it, but those records expressly lack supervisor sign-off and do not alter assessed priority (S-021, S-022, S-025, S-026).
7. A paraphrase of Sandra's missing 4 August email and Meeting 4 notes point to a comparative deterministic-versus-learned RSU load-management study and to identifying the conditions in which each approach performs better (S-011, S-012). Because both are class C and the original email is missing, this is retained as a SHOULD/open decision rather than a new MUST.
8. Randy's direct Q&A authoritatively settles technical semantics within his environment: the so-called concurrent limit is an admission/in-flight waiting-room ceiling, not compute capacity; surplus tasks are rejected without entering the queue; several further controller ideas remain suggestions (S-007).
9. TfGM confirmed only a conditional access path and possible availability; National Highways confirmed portal access and licence terms, not delivery of the requested measured feed. Neither exchange establishes a real-Manchester-data product requirement (S-005, S-006, S-017, S-018).

## Adjudication record

R1 and R2 independently agreed on the five Project 237 core obligations, the formal evaluation/report/video and conditional ethics duties, the authority boundary between Sandra and Randy, the corrected queue semantics, the optional status of the platform, and the absence of proof for live/real Manchester data, forecasting, SUMO, UI pages, user study, or agentic AI as core requirements.

Their only material differences were presentation and consolidation. R1 separated academic traceability from evaluation and included the secondary Randy permission record in a conditional provenance candidate; R2 folded traceability into evaluation/claim accuracy and limited provider obligations to primary A/B terms. This baseline adopts R2's narrower authority boundary: academic traceability is consolidated into TT-REQ-006 and TT-REQ-010, provider compliance uses S-005/S-006, and Randy's withheld permission remains an unresolved decision rather than an active requirement based on unseen wording. R1 characterised honest real/synthetic separation as SHOULD or potentially MUST; R2 characterised claim accuracy as MUST. The latter is adopted because the authoritative rubric explicitly assesses technical accuracy and evidence-supported conclusions (S-003), while the detailed UI/mechanism for provenance remains unconstrained.

Neither analysis promoted the late RSU direction to MUST. It is retained as TT-REQ-008, SHOULD, Open decision YES. Neither analysis treated the owner-selected platform as supervisor-agreed core. It is retained only as TT-REQ-014, MAY.

# A. CORE PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS

## TT-REQ-001

**Requirement ID:**  
TT-REQ-001

**Title:**  
Justified ITS resource-management methodology

**Canonical wording:**  
"TrafficTwin shall embody and document a suitable, justified methodology for assessing and improving resource management for data-intensive ITS services."

**Priority:**  
MUST

**Requirement type:**  
PRODUCT OUTCOME

**Primary stakeholder:**  
Dr Sandra Sampaio as Project 237 proposer; University assessment authority for justification.

**Source basis:**

- S-001
- S-003

**Negotiation history:**  
Project 237 deliverable A formally requires investigation of a suitable methodology. The assessment rubric requires the chosen methods, their suitability, reasoning, and alternatives to be explained. No later source removes this obligation.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A named methodology is documented and explicitly linked to the Project 237 resource-management objectives.
- Its methods, assumptions, alternatives, and suitability are justified.
- The evaluation design can answer the stated resource-management questions.

**Evidence required to claim satisfaction:**  
Dissertation methodology text, traceable method/configuration artifacts, and evaluation outputs showing that the documented method was actually used.

**Out of scope:**  
No particular algorithm, framework, cloud provider, UI, simulator, or named experiment family is mandated.

**Dependencies:**  
The final specialised research question must be declared; its supervisor approval is currently incomplete.

**Confidence:**  
HIGH

**Open decision:**  
NO

**Superseded formulations:**  
None found. Later specialisations may instantiate this requirement but have not replaced it.

## TT-REQ-002

**Requirement ID:**  
TT-REQ-002

**Title:**

**Canonical wording:**

**Priority:**  
MUST

**Requirement type:**  
PRODUCT OUTCOME

**Primary stakeholder:**  
Dr Sandra Sampaio as Project 237 proposer.

**Negotiation history:**

**Acceptance criteria:**

- More than one clearly differentiated ITS service use case is designed and implemented; for audit purposes, the minimum operational interpretation is two while the source ambiguity around "a few" is declared.
- Each use case states its service purpose, workload/input, resource needs, and relevant QoS outcomes.
- Each use case has observable executable or generated behavior sufficient to support the investigation.

**Evidence required to claim satisfaction:**  
Reachable use-case entry points or reproducible executions, representative inputs, generated outputs, and tests or direct probes demonstrating behavior.

**Out of scope:**  
The brief does not mandate Manchester, VEC, journey-time prediction, forecasting, SUMO, live data, or a digital-twin UI as the specific use cases.

TT-REQ-001; the selected use cases must be relevant to the resource-management objectives.

NO

# B. DISSERTATION DEMONSTRATION REQUIREMENTS

## TT-REQ-006

**Requirement ID:**  
TT-REQ-006

**Title:**  
Goal-aligned evaluation and evidence-supported conclusions

**Canonical wording:**  
"TrafficTwin shall be evaluated, tested, or critically reflected upon using justified methods aligned with the stated project goals, and every material conclusion shall be supported by the resulting evidence."

**Negotiation history:**  
The rubric formally requires justified evaluation/testing/reflection aligned with project goals and conclusions supported by outcomes. **Acceptance criteria:**

- Objectives, evaluation questions, methods, evidence, and conclusions are traceable to one another.
- Evaluation-method choices and relevant alternatives are justified.
- Negative results, failures, uncertainty, confounders, and limitations are reported where material.
- Conclusions do not exceed what the evidence demonstrates.

**Evidence required to claim satisfaction:**  
The dissertation/report, cited literature, evaluation plan, executed outputs, analysis, and a trace from each material conclusion to supporting evidence.

**Out of scope:**  
No particular statistical test, seed count, user study, experiment-lane name, or requirement for a positive result is imposed.

**Dependencies:**  
TT-REQ-001 and the final declared project objectives.

HIGH

NO

## TT-REQ-008

**Requirement ID:**  
TT-REQ-008

**Title:**  
Comparative infrastructure-side RSU load-management investigation

**Canonical wording:**  
"TrafficTwin shall, if the late RSU research direction is confirmed, support comparison of the existing vehicle-side offloading arrangement with a deterministic/rule-based infrastructure-side load-management approach and a separately defined learned scheduling/load-management approach, identifying the operating conditions in which each approach performs better."

**Priority:**  
SHOULD

VALIDATION

Reportedly Dr Sandra Sampaio for dissertation direction; Randy Prasetia Putra only for relevant technical semantics.

**Requirement ID:**  
TT-REQ-009

**Title:**  
Varied, controlled, non-trivial comparative scenarios

# C. QUALITY AND DEFENSIBILITY REQUIREMENTS

## TT-REQ-010

**Requirement ID:**  
TT-REQ-010

**Title:**  
Technically accurate and honestly bounded evidence claims

**Canonical wording:**  
"TrafficTwin shall make technically accurate, evidence-backed claims and shall explicitly distinguish observed provider data, simulated mobility, and synthetic or assumed task/RSU inputs; it shall not present a Manchester label or provider account as proof of real Manchester VEC validation."

**Priority:**  
MUST

**Requirement type:**  
QUALITY

**Primary stakeholder:**  
University assessment authority; Dr Sandra Sampaio for the mixed-real/synthetic case boundary.

**Source basis:**

- S-003
- S-007
- S-011
- S-005
- S-006
- S-017
- S-018

**Negotiation history:**  
The rubric explicitly assesses technical accuracy and evidence-supported conclusions. Meeting 4 states that traffic data may ground vehicle mobility while task demand and RSU details still have to be fabricated, producing a partly realistic scenario. Provider records prove access conditions or possible availability, not delivered measured data. Randy confirms that experimental scaling conventions are not physical claims.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Every material dataset/input and output is labelled as observed, simulated, synthetic, mixed, or unavailable with its provenance.
- Claims such as "live," "current," "real Manchester," and "validated" do not exceed the demonstrated evidence layer.

- Limitations and unavailable evidence are explicit in product-facing outputs and dissertation claims where relevant.

**Evidence required to claim satisfaction:**  
Dataset provenance and standing, source identifiers, product/report labels, representative outputs, and a claim-to-evidence review.

**Out of scope:**  
This requirement does not mandate real Manchester data, a live feed, or a particular provenance UI.

**Dependencies:**  
Applies whenever data, geography, realism, validation, or experimental results are claimed.

**Confidence:**  
HIGH for technical accuracy and evidence-bounded claims; MEDIUM for the exact Manchester dataset Sandra intended.

**Open decision:**  
NO

**Superseded formulations:**

## TT-REQ-011

**Requirement ID:**  
TT-REQ-011

**Title:**  
Correct RSU admission and compute semantics

**Canonical wording:**  
"TrafficTwin shall, whenever it uses Randy's environment or results, distinguish the per-RSU admission/in-flight waiting-room ceiling from compute service rate or worker capacity, preserve terminal rejection of surplus tasks outside the RSU queue, and avoid describing an admission-limit change as a processing-capacity change."

**Priority:**  
MUST

**Requirement type:**  
QUALITY

**Primary stakeholder:**  
Randy Prasetia Putra as technical producer; reportedly adopted by Dr Sandra Sampaio.

**Source basis:**

- S-007
- S-012 (secondary supervisor corroboration)

**Negotiation history:**  
Randy directly confirms that the quantity counts waiting plus served tasks, is unrelated to processing power, and should be called a per-RSU admission/in-flight ceiling. He also confirms immediate terminal rejection with no retry/fallback/re-forwarding and that rejected work never enters the queue. His proposed detailed event ledger remains optional.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Definitions, configuration names, units, UI/report text, and analysis keep admission limit separate from compute/service capacity.
- Surplus tasks are rejected immediately and never enter an RSU queue in any claimed reproduction of Randy's semantics.
- Prior or current findings do not attribute an admission-clamp effect to compute scaling.
- Any alternative semantics are explicitly labelled as a new model, not Randy's confirmed environment.

**Evidence required to claim satisfaction:**  
Configuration/schema definitions, public/report terminology, targeted boundary probes, queue/rejection traces, and corrected analysis of affected experiments.

**Out of scope:**  
Per-task ledger fields, two-population reporting, action masking, exact backhaul, staleness sweeps, proactive scaling, and DLA are not required merely because Randy suggested them.

**Dependencies:**  
Triggered only if Randy's environment, data, or reported results are used or reproduced.

**Confidence:**  
HIGH for technical semantics; MEDIUM for supervisor adoption.

**Open decision:**  
NO

**Superseded formulations:**  
`RSU_MAX_CONCURRENT` interpreted as processing capacity, and the generic "3.3 times capacity reduction" interpretation, are superseded by S-007's direct correction.

TT-REQ-013

**Title:**  
Ethics and information-governance gate

NO

## Baseline authority and interpretation

This is the single source-derived baseline for the TrafficTwin v0.8 traceability audit. It describes the negotiated MSc/project obligations that can be defended from the accessible evidence; it is not a union of product ideas and it does not derive requirements from implementation.

The official Project 237 brief remains the only authoritative substantive project scope and has not been shown to be formally superseded (S-001). Later supervisor notes plausibly specialise that scope toward comparative RSU load management, but the decisive 4 August Outlook email is unavailable and the surviving records are class C (S-011, S-012). Accordingly, the formal brief remains MUST, the late RSU specialisation is SHOULD with an open decision, and the data-engineering/what-if platform is MAY because the latest accessible platform-specific supervisor note places it after the scientific work, if time permits (S-008–S-010).

Priority terms have their ordinary audit meaning: MUST is required by authoritative or confirmed evidence, including explicitly triggered legal/ethical/semantic constraints; SHOULD is a well-supported expected outcome whose final authority or minimum scope remains incomplete; MAY is optional. A conditional MUST is evaluated only when its stated trigger occurs.

## Included source record

- Complete corpus considered: S-001 through S-034 (34 unique sources: 5 A, 2 B, 7 C, 14 D, 6 E).
- Direct active-requirement basis: S-001, S-002, S-003, S-004, S-005, S-006, S-007, S-008, S-009, S-010, S-011, S-012, S-017, S-018.

## Concise negotiation history

1. The 27 May 2026 official Project 237 brief established a resource-management-centred ITS project: investigate a suitable methodology, implement a few ITS use cases, profile their run-time behaviour, assess existing cloud resource-management strategies against service/QoS needs, and propose improved dynamic strategies across devices and clouds (S-001).
2. Official programme material added assessment, report/video, evaluation, technical-accuracy, and conditional ethics obligations, not TrafficTwin product features (S-002–S-004).
3. Early supervision explored alternatives. A heterogeneous traffic data-engineering/current-view/forecasting/what-if platform was initially only a possibility; a Manchester digital-twin-style app was later described as a candidate while task offloading versus journey-time prediction remained undecided (S-008, S-009).
4. Randy proposed monitoring, dashboard, explainability, and resource-advice ideas but expressly conditioned development on Sandra's approval; no acceptance of that complete product concept is evidenced (S-015, S-016).
5. Meeting 3 prioritised scientific explanation and validation of the counter-intuitive experiment and demoted the data platform to a small extension after the core work, if time remained (S-010).
6. Abdulla subsequently chose the platform as a product-owner direction, and internal designs elaborated it, but those records expressly lack supervisor sign-off and do not alter assessed priority (S-021, S-022, S-025, S-026).
7. A paraphrase of Sandra's missing 4 August email and Meeting 4 notes point to a comparative deterministic-versus-learned RSU load-management study and to identifying the conditions in which each approach performs better (S-011, S-012). Because both are class C and the original email is missing, this is retained as a SHOULD/open decision rather than a new MUST.
8. Randy's direct Q&A authoritatively settles technical semantics within his environment: the so-called concurrent limit is an admission/in-flight waiting-room ceiling, not compute capacity; surplus tasks are rejected without entering the queue; several further controller ideas remain suggestions (S-007).
9. TfGM confirmed only a conditional access path and possible availability; National Highways confirmed portal access and licence terms, not delivery of the requested measured feed. Neither exchange establishes a real-Manchester-data product requirement (S-005, S-006, S-017, S-018).

## Adjudication record

R1 and R2 independently agreed on the five Project 237 core obligations, the formal evaluation/report/video and conditional ethics duties, the authority boundary between Sandra and Randy, the corrected queue semantics, the optional status of the platform, and the absence of proof for live/real Manchester data, forecasting, SUMO, UI pages, user study, or agentic AI as core requirements.

Their only material differences were presentation and consolidation. R1 separated academic traceability from evaluation and included the secondary Randy permission record in a conditional provenance candidate; R2 folded traceability into evaluation/claim accuracy and limited provider obligations to primary A/B terms. This baseline adopts R2's narrower authority boundary: academic traceability is consolidated into TT-REQ-006 and TT-REQ-010, provider compliance uses S-005/S-006, and Randy's withheld permission remains an unresolved decision rather than an active requirement based on unseen wording. R1 characterised honest real/synthetic separation as SHOULD or potentially MUST; R2 characterised claim accuracy as MUST. The latter is adopted because the authoritative rubric explicitly assesses technical accuracy and evidence-supported conclusions (S-003), while the detailed UI/mechanism for provenance remains unconstrained.

Neither analysis promoted the late RSU direction to MUST. It is retained as TT-REQ-008, SHOULD, Open decision YES. Neither analysis treated the owner-selected platform as supervisor-agreed core. It is retained only as TT-REQ-014, MAY.
